title: Delineation of areas having elevated electrical conductivity, orientation and characterization of bedrock fractures, and occurrence of groundwater discharge to surface water at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Barite Hill/Nevada Goldfields Superfund site near McCormick, South Carolina
citation: Chapman, M.J., Huffman, B.A., and McSwain, K.B., 2015, Delineation of areas having elevated electrical conductivity, orientation and characterization of bedrock fractures, and occurrence of groundwater discharge to surface water at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Barite Hill/Nevada Goldfields Superfund site near McCormick, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2015-5084, map scale 1:13,300.
notes: Wells from table 1 (pages 18-19) with table 2 water-quality profile averages (page 25). The lithologic logs of wells BH65, BH66 and BH67 (figures 10-12) were not recorded: the page images show the interval boundaries but the lithology patterns are not rendered, so no interval can be tied to a lithology; the legends were not recorded. The EM-induction depths of high conductivity (about 72 ft in BH33/BH34, about 110 ft in BH51) are geophysical, not geologic surfaces, and were not recorded as surfaces. Regolith thickness 28-57 ft is inferred by the authors from casing depths (page 27); no surface recorded. Water-quality ranges in the abstract and text duplicate table 2 and were not recorded again. pH values have no units printed.
